outcomeNote: A mishna stating the four seasons of judgment with one prooftext.

segments.he: מַתְנִי׳ בְּאַרְבָּעָה פְּרָקִים הָעוֹלָם נִידּוֹן: בַּפֶּסַח — עַל הַתְּבוּאָה, בַּעֲצֶרֶת — עַל פֵּירוֹת הָאִילָן, בְּרֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה — כׇּל בָּאֵי עוֹלָם עוֹבְרִין לְפָנָיו כִּבְנֵי מָרוֹן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״הַיּוֹצֵר יַחַד לִבָּם הַמֵּבִין אֶל כׇּל מַעֲשֵׂיהֶם״, וּבֶחָג נִידּוֹנִין עַל הַמַּיִם.
segments.en: «MISHNA:» «At four times» of the year «the world is judged: On Passover» judgment is passed «concerning grain; on Shavuot concerning fruits» that grow on «a tree; on Rosh HaShana all creatures pass before Him like sheep [benei maron], as it is stated: “He Who fashions their hearts alike, Who considers all their deeds”» (Psalms 33:15); «and on the festival» of Sukkot «they are judged concerning water,» i.e., the rainfall of the coming year.

moves.summary: the world is judged at four times of the year
Psalms 33:15 supports that all creatures pass before Him on Rosh HaShana
moves.about: all creatures pass before God like sheep on Rosh HaShana

positions.claim: the world is judged at four seasons: Passover for grain, Shavuot for tree fruit, Rosh HaShana for all creatures, Sukkot for water
